Definition: from G94; (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act):--iniquity, unjust, unrighteousness, wrong.
BiblicalUsage: Adikia is unrighteousness — wrongfulness as a quality and as an act, the opposite of what is right before God. Jesus tells of the unjust steward, Paul says God's wrath is revealed against all unrighteousness, and John says all unrighteousness is sin. It is one of the New Testament's broadest words for evil, covering unjust deeds, unjust character, and unjust systems alike.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe adikia matters because it names sin for what it is: not just mistakes, but wrongness — things out of line with God's righteousness. And the same Scriptures that name it also name the cure: Christ, who became our righteousness, so that the unrighteous can stand right before God.
